A "good string" T is defined as having exactly one pair of consecutive characters that are the same. The transformation involves flipping characters in S, with each flip having an associated cost. The goal is to compute the minimum total cost required to achieve this transformation.
fix_specification_reasoning.diagnosis_and_repair_directions: The flawed specification incorrectly initializes a 3-dimensional dp array with dimensions [N][2][2]. This is unnecessary and overly complex for the problem at hand. The dp array should instead be a 2-dimensional array with dimensions [N][2], where the second dimension represents the cost of making the i-th character of S either '0' or '1'. The dp array should track the minimum cost to achieve a "good string" up to each character position. The final output should be the minimum cost to make the entire string a "good string," which is not correctly specified in the output section of the flawed specification.
